<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`, touching **14** documentable anchor(s).

**39** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4c32b9694b7b248646b2053b6eafea2cc212693b`.

⛔ **8** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `created_at (literal, 43 pages)`
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **4** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4c32b9694b7b248646b2053b6eafea2cc212693b` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `00d5640e2921ea1a3d6f8dedcd54af232caa5f8b` — the merge of head `4593c1d0df206e3833da00e4278177b6f2cf634a` into base `4c32b9694b7b248646b2053b6eafea2cc212693b`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 00d5640e2921ea1a3d6f8dedcd54af232caa5f8b && git checkout 00d5640e2921ea1a3d6f8dedcd54af232caa5f8b
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 4c32b9694b7b248646b2053b6eafea2cc212693b 4593c1d0df206e3833da00e4278177b6f2cf634a && git checkout -B drift-repro 4c32b9694b7b248646b2053b6eafea2cc212693b && git merge --no-ff 4593c1d0df206e3833da00e4278177b6f2cf634a

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4c32b9694b7b248646b2053b6eafea2cc212693b
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 4c32b9694b7b248646b2053b6eafea2cc212693b` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `533eb60bdb742250584353fba3e50d5d17dccf13`
Local-runs: none

PR #33434 for card #33246, on the declaration face. Read: the card body and its seven comments (6879098956, 6879740792, 6880234097, 6880862710, 6883467822, 6884094895, 6884116702), the PR body, its three-path file list, the net diff against `main` (`2797f81d`, merge base `fc283d6d`), merged PR #33205 and its two records (6870963898, 6878859677) for the reading this PR extends, and the head's check-runs. Every statement about behaviour below is read from the tree. Nothing was built or run.

**Check-runs on the head, read on 2026-11-14:** 63 runs: 22 success, 11 skipped, 30 in progress, none failed. `Check Changeset`, `PR-body guards`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates` and `Check PR Size` are green. Every `Test Core` shard, `Build Core`, the three `Type Check` jobs and most `Lint` jobs had no conclusion yet. ⛔ This record does not stand in for them.

**One must-fix (F1), two should-fix (F2, F3), two nits (N1, N2).**

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The flow and hook publish doors stop refusing an unguarded ordering or arithmetic operand over an injected column the object does not declare.** Right as declared, and a widening. The strip (`validate-expressions.ts:2385`) runs before every index, `buildNullableFieldIndex` (`:570`) then sees declared fields only, and the three flow sites and both hook forms reach `checkNullGuards` against that index.
2. **Nothing that published before is refused.** Right, by reading.
   - Names: `buildFieldIndex` (`:221`) re-adds every stripped name through `injectedColumnsFor`, which reads the same plan the strip reads (`injectedSystemColumnDefs`), so no injected column becomes an unknown field. A column the registry injects outside that plan is not stripped and stays as it was.
   - Types and nullability: a missing type is `dyn` and a missing nullable entry is no verdict. Both only remove findings.
   - The other readers of the stripped objects: `storedMetadataBodyReferencesOf` (the injected lookups point at `sys_user`, `sys_organization` and `sys_business_unit`, none a stored-metadata-body table), `unprovisionedInjectedColumnsFor` (an absent anchor and an identical one get the same provenance, so the `external` advisory is unchanged), `buildAttachedOnReadIndex`, `bulkConfirmTextIssues` and `actionCopyTemplateIssues` (neither reads `fields`). The `view` and `page` early returns sit before the strip.
   - The differential: baseline, candidate and stored universe run the same function with the same write type, so findings on context objects still cancel.
3. **"The only verdicts that move are the flow and hook null-guard findings" and "type verdicts are the same before and after" (PR body, Measurement and 速读).** Wrong. See F1.
4. **`os build`, `os validate`, `os lint` and MCP `validate_expression` are unchanged.** Right. The build passes no write type, and `judgeAuthoredSiteExpression` already stripped (`authored-site-expression.ts:235`).
5. **No exported type or signature changes.** Right. One statement inside `runStackExpressionPasses` and one docblock sentence.
6. **`Metadata-protocol: added`.** Defensible. See N1.

**F1, must-fix. The strip also empties the type index of the injected columns at every runtime door, so the hook, flow, action and object doors stop giving type verdicts they gave on `main`. These were true refusals, and the PR states that none moves.**

- **Mechanism.** `buildFieldTypeIndex` (`:432`) reads declared fields only; its docblock says an injected column is left `dyn`. On `main` the door's objects are served, so `created_at` and `updated_at` are in that index as `datetime` and `queue` as `text` (`AUDIT_FIELD_DEFS`, `QUEUE_FIELD_DEF`). `check` (`:2716`) hands the index to `validateExpression`, where `datetime` is typed `timestamp` (`packages/formula/src/validate.ts:372`) and date arithmetic is a hard error (`typeSoundnessIssue`, `dateTextIssue`). After the strip the index holds none of them, and `firstTypeMismatch` returns early on an all-`dyn` record.
- **Inputs, by reading.**
  - Hook `condition` (record scope, `:4306`): `record.created_at + 1 > 0` (`date-arith`), `record.updated_at - record.created_at > duration('1h')` (`date-text-arithmetic`, the #28944 shape), `record.queue > 5` (`type-mismatch-fail-closed`). On `main` the hook door refuses each with `expression-invalid`. At this head it publishes each.
  - Flow condition (flattened scope): the bare `created_at + 1 > 0`. Same split.
  - Action `visible` / `disabled` (`checkAction` goes through `check`): same split. The PR says action writes do not move.
  - Object write: a field rule slot that reads `parent.` over a served master (`masterTypes`, `:3807`) loses the master's injected types. Lower confidence; not traced to an input.
- **Why it matters.** Unlike the null-guard on `created_at`, these door verdicts were correct: the runtime holds a date as text and the arithmetic faults, so the flow run fails or the hook condition faults. `os build` never gave them only because its type index does not cover injected columns. A Studio author has no build step, so the door was the only gate that told them.
- **What is false as written.** The PR body's Measurement ("type verdicts ... are the same before and after", "the only verdicts that move"), the 速读 risk line, and the dev report's summary. The changeset's `Clause-②` line and Now paragraph name the null-guard only. Record 6878859677 ① item 4 named this same effect for the extension door, so it was known for this strip.
- **Why the pins and the measurement miss it.** The eight measured conditions hold a type mismatch on `created_at` that is an ordering, which a date tolerates. No case holds date arithmetic or a text column.
- **Basis.** Read, not run. One case settles it: at the gate, a hook write with `record.created_at + 1 > 0` over `applyInjectedSystemColumns(account)`, on `main` and at the head.
- **Remedy, the dev's choice.**
  - Keep the door's type verdicts: apply the as-authored reading to the nullable index alone, and leave the type index on the served objects at the non-extension doors.
  - Or keep the one strip and declare the loss: name the dropped type verdicts in the changeset and the PR body, correct the Measurement, and file the card that makes the build type the injected columns (their definitions are in `@objectstack/spec/data` since #8116, which the `buildFieldTypeIndex` docblock predates).
  - Either way, pin the chosen verdict at the gate.

### ② Semver level

- The changeset moves `@objectstack/lint` at `minor`. `packages/lint` is the only released package the diff moves, and the kind `added` takes at least `minor`. The level follows the declared kind. `Check Changeset` is green.
- `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: added` stand line-initial on the PR body and the changeset body. The arm is right: nothing is newly refused (① item 2). No BREAKING banner or ADR-0087 marker is owed for a widening.
- The bound the `Clause-②` line states is exceeded: the door also accepts conditions it refused for a type fault (F1). The line must name what the diff publishes.
- `skip-changeset` is not used. Right: the diff publishes.

**N1, nit. `Metadata-protocol: added` against AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist 3.** The checklist calls a newly accepted value `added`. The schema and `os build` accepted this value already; only the publish door changes. `added` with `minor` is the reading that follows the door author, and `none` with `patch` (a bug fix in a released package) is the reading that follows the authorable language. No changeset on `main` is a door-only widening of this kind, so there is no precedent either way, and the gates pass both. `added` is the wider declaration and costs nothing here: `@objectstack/lint` is in the fixed group, which other pending changesets already move at `minor`. Accepted as declared.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Dev report `open_questions` 1** (per-column nullability): answered by the seat in 6884116702, option B, card #33435 (open, `domain:spec`, p3). Answered. One point for the seat stays open: F2.
- **Out-of-scope note 1** (`flows.mdx` item 5): accepted as noted. The sentence stays true.
- **Out-of-scope note 2** (a hop leaf through an injected lookup): recorded on #33435. Confirmed by reading: the written object's own body arrives stripped, so `refuseUndeclaredHopField` never saw `owner_id` on the subject.
- **Deviation: the strip covers every runtime write, not the flow and hook walks alone.** This is where F1 comes from. The one-reading argument holds for the nullable index; it does not hold for the type index, where the door was the truthful side.
- **Deviation: door pins in the lint package; the real-door measurement was a deleted probe.** See F3.
- **Deviation: model-free commit trailers.** Not a contract matter.
- **Claim 6883467822, provisional `Clause-②: yes (widening)`:** the arm stands; the bound does not (F1). **Provisional `Metadata-protocol`:** stated as `added` (N1).
- **File surface:** three paths, all inside the claim. No breach.
- **Gates not measured by the dev** (`check:dual-build-cjs-loads`): CI's, and without a conclusion at this record.

**F2, should-fix, escalated to the seat. The door newly accepts five columns the dev measured NULL on a stored row, and the follow-up will refuse them again.**

- The dev's own measurement: `owner_id`, `created_by`, `updated_by`, `owning_business_unit_id` and `queue` hold NULL after a system-context insert. Triage's premise (6879098956: an injected column is never null on a stored record) holds for `created_at` and `updated_at` only.
- On `main` the door's null-guard on those five was a true refusal. This PR publishes their acceptance, and #33435's candidate fix is `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` with an ADR-0087 entry. So the path is a widening now and a BREAKING narrowing later, for a verdict the door already had right.
- The changeset names `owner_id` among the accepted columns and does not say it can be NULL.
- Remedy: either limit this PR's acceptance to the columns measured never-null and leave the rest to #33435, or keep B and add the sentence to the changeset so the published record says what is knowingly accepted. The seat's call; B is a seat answer, not a maintainer ruling.

**F3, should-fix. No committed case reads the object as the registry serves it at the real door.**

- The new describe feeds the gate `applyInjectedSystemColumns(account)`. The strip matches a column only when it is key for key the platform's definition (`isInjectedColumnDefinition`). If `applySystemFields` ever adds a key, the strip stops matching at the real door, the refusal returns, and these pins stay green.
- PR #33205 answered the same gap with real-door cases in `packages/runtime`. Here `packages/runtime` is outside the claimed surface, so the dev disclosed the deviation.
- Remedy: one real-door case (a flow and a hook over a registered object, `saveMetaItem` then `publishMetaItem`), in this PR with a surface amendment or as a follow-up card. The seat's call.

**N2, nit.** The PARITY case on `owner_id`, `created_by` and `owning_business_unit_id` asserts the door equals the build, whatever the build says. It will stay green through #33435 in either direction, which is its stated purpose, and it pins no verdict of its own.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `ddd834f5bddc6cce244fc3d162c99d4ecdb76015`
Local-runs: none

Round 2 on PR #33434 for card #33246, on the declaration face. Round 1 is record 6884221427 at `533eb60b` (FAIL); the seat's rulings and the surface amendment are 6884227999; the dev's round-2 report is 6884768478. Read: the card body and its nine comments, the PR body and its two comments, the four-path file list, the net diff against `main` (`7e61983e`, merge base `fc283d6d`; no file the diff or this record cites moved between the two), and the head's check-runs. Every statement about behaviour below is read from the tree. Nothing was built or run.

**Check-runs on the head, read on 2026-11-14:** 70 runs: 57 success, 13 skipped, none failed, none pending. Every `Test Core` shard, `Build Core`, the `Type Check` jobs, `Check Changeset`, `PR-body guards`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates` and `Check PR Size` are green. The new runtime door file and the lint describe are inside `Test Core`.

**One must-fix (M1), one should-fix (S1), three nits (N3, N4, N5).**

**Round-1 findings at this head:**

- **F1 (must-fix): resolved at the hook and action doors and for a flow's bare spelling; not resolved at the flow door for a `record.`-rooted read.** See M1.
- **F2 (should-fix): resolved.** Only `created_at` and `updated_at` leave the door's nullable index; the five stay; the changeset names the five and #33435.
- **F3 (should-fix): resolved.** The runtime file goes through the real door.
- **N2 (nit): resolved.** The parity case is gone; each verdict is pinned.
- **N1 (nit): stands as ruled.** Declarations kept as filed.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The type index is back on the served objects at every door but the extension door.** Right. The strip statement (`validate-expressions.ts:2429`) is byte for byte `main`'s (`extensionWrite` only); the diff adds a comment sentence there and nothing else. `buildFieldTypeIndex(typedObjects)` (`:2446`) therefore reads what it read on `main`, so the hook and action doors keep `date arithmetic` on `record.created_at + 1 > 0`, and the flow door keeps it on the bare `created_at + 1 > 0`. Pinned at the gate (the third LIT of the lint describe).
2. **Only the nullable index changes, and only for the two stamped columns.** Right. `buildNullableFieldIndex(typedObjects, { platformStamped })` (`:2447`) is the one call; `platformStamped` is `options.runtimeWriteType !== undefined`. The skip (`isPlatformStampedColumn`, `:601`) needs all of: the name is `created_at` or `updated_at`; `platformProvisionsStorage(obj)`; the object's own plan holds the column (`injectedSystemColumnDefs(obj)[fname]`); the served definition is key for key the platform's (`isInjectedColumnDefinition`).
   - `owner_id`, `created_by`, `updated_by`, `owning_business_unit_id`, `queue` (and `organization_id`, see N3) stay in the index as on `main`.
   - `id` is in the ruling's list and not in the code's set. Right: `injectedSystemColumnDefs` never puts `id` in a field map, so there is no entry to skip.
3. **The skip cannot be spoofed into dropping a guard that is owed.** Right, by reading each way an author could reach it:
   - A `created_at` declared with any key that differs (own label, a missing key, an extra key): the equality fails, the column stays judged. Pinned (CONTROL, "Opened").
   - A `created_at` declared key for key as the platform's, on an object whose plan holds the audit family: it is the platform's column. The save path strips it (`stripServedSystemColumns`, before the gate) and the registry injects it back; the audit stamp writes it by name. No guard is wrongly dropped.
   - The same declaration on an object that opts the audit family out (`systemFields: false`, `systemFields.audit: false`, `managedBy: 'better-auth'`): the plan has no entry, so `injected === undefined` and the column stays judged.
   - An `external` object: `platformProvisionsStorage` is false, the column stays judged. Pinned (CONTROL).
   - An array-shaped `fields`: each definition carries `name`, the key count differs, the column stays judged. The conservative direction.
   - A field two packages tie on is not in `typedObjects` at all, as on `main`.
4. **Nothing that published before is refused.** Right. The skip only removes names from a set. `checkNullGuards` (`:2647`) and the flow's `nullGuardBare` (`:3122`) read that set, and a shorter set only removes findings; a start condition's proofs for the other fields are unchanged.
5. **The verdicts that move are the flow and hook null-guard findings on the two columns.** Right for the site kinds: the index's other readers are a validation rule (`:3730`) and a field `requiredWhen` (`:4075`), both on an `object` write, where the written body arrives stripped (`protocol-save.ts`, the strip precedes the gate), and where flows and hooks are not walked. Context objects cancel in the differential, as before. **Wrong for what moves inside the flow door:** see M1.
6. **`os build`, `os validate`, `os lint` and MCP `validate_expression` are unchanged.** Right. The build passes no write type, so its index is what it was. `judgeAuthoredSiteExpression` does pass a write type, and strips first with the same identity test, so the skip finds nothing there.
7. **No exported type or signature changes.** Right. One private constant, one private function, one optional parameter on a private function, three more named imports from `@objectstack/spec/data`.
8. **The runtime file goes through the real door.** Right. `better-sqlite3` behind the real `ObjectQL`, the real `sys_metadata` objects, `ObjectStackProtocolImplementation`, the account registered through `registerApp`, each item saved as a draft and published through `publishMetaItem`. It asserts the row state (`active` / `draft`), the 422 `INVALID_METADATA` and the one `expression-invalid` issue naming `record.owner_id`, and that the registry's served definition and a stored row are what the lint pins assume. One case per site kind, as ruled.

**M1, must-fix. At the flow door a `record.`-rooted date arithmetic on `created_at` / `updated_at` is now published. `main` refused it, ruling F1 names it, and the changeset says it is still refused.**

- **Input.** A record-triggered flow whose start condition, edge condition or `decision` branch is `record.created_at + 1 > 0` or `record.updated_at - record.created_at > duration('1h')` (the two F1 spellings, with `record.`).
- **On `main`.** Refused, by the null-guard alone: `+` and `-` are in `FAULTING_BINARY_OPS` (`validate-null-guards.ts`), `record.created_at` is in the served object's nullable set, and `checkFlowNullGuards` reports it. The type verdict does not see it: at a flattened site the record-root pass is for the text and boolean mismatch only ("The date verdicts stay the bare name's alone", `packages/formula/src/cel-engine.ts:1361`), and `firstDateTextVerdict` types no record root there (`:1489`).
- **At this head.** The null-guard finding is gone and nothing replaces it, so the flow publishes. The runtime holds the column as its ISO text and the arithmetic faults, so the run fails (the same fault the hook door still refuses).
- **Ruling F1** (6884227999): those conditions "stay refused at the hook, flow and action doors exactly as on `main`". Held at the hook and the action. At the flow it holds for the bare spelling only.
- **What is false as written.**
  - The changeset's Unchanged paragraph: "date arithmetic such as `record.created_at + 1 > 0` is still refused". False at the flow door, for the spelling it quotes.
  - The changeset's and the PR body's `Clause-②` line: "no other verdict moves". And its "ordering or arithmetic operator": at a hook or an action the arithmetic is still refused by the type verdict, so the one place the arithmetic acceptance is real is this one.
  - The PR body's Acceptance note and the report's out-of-scope note ("not type-checked at the door on `main` or here ... noted, not changed"). True about the type verdict, and it leaves out that the door's verdict on the input moves from refused to published.
- **Why the pins miss it.** The flow rows of the F1 pin use the bare spelling; the `record.` spelling is pinned at the hook and the action only. The Measurement table's arithmetic row lists hook and action.
- **Basis.** Read, not run. One case settles it: at the gate, the describe's `flowAt('start', 'record.created_at + 1 > 0')` over the served account, on `main` and at the head.
- **Remedy, the dev's choice within the ruling.**
  - Keep the refusal: the skip applies to an ordering operand only, so an arithmetic operand on the two columns keeps its null-guard finding at every site. Nothing true is lost: arithmetic on a date column is refused at the hook and the action already. Pin the `record.` spelling at a flow slot, red against this head.
  - Or the seat rules the loss accepted: the changeset and the PR body then say that a flow's `record.`-rooted date arithmetic on the two columns is no longer refused, and a card carries the flattened record-root date verdict in `packages/formula` (a narrowing, outside this surface).

### ② Semver level

- The changeset moves `@objectstack/lint` at `minor`, the only released package the diff moves (`packages/runtime` gains a test file only). The level follows the declared kind `added`. `Check Changeset` is green.
- `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: added` stand line-initial on the PR body and the changeset body. The arm is right: nothing is newly refused (① item 4). No BREAKING banner or ADR-0087 marker is owed.
- The bound the `Clause-②` line states is not what the diff publishes at the flow door (M1). The line and the Unchanged paragraph must say what is true.
- The door/build note is true as far as it goes: on the five named columns the door refuses an unguarded ordering and the build judges none, and #33435 is named. It is one column short (N3).
- `Metadata-protocol: added`: as ruled under N1; the F2 change does not alter it.
- `skip-changeset` is not used. Right: the diff publishes.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Report 6884768478 `open_questions`:** empty. Round 1's question was answered in 6884116702 (option B, #33435).
- **Out-of-scope note** (a flow's `record.created_at + 1 > 0` is not type-checked): not accepted as noted. It is M1.
- **Deviation: the PR body and title handed to the seat.** The body on the PR is the round-2 body and carries both declaration lines. Not a contract matter.
- **Deviation: the two stamped names spelled in lint.** Accepted. Lint may not import `@objectstack/objectql`; the docblock names `sys_stamp_audit_insert` and `PLATFORM_PROVISIONED_COLUMNS`, both read on `main` and both agree; the runtime file pins the stored row against the real engine.
- **File surface:** four paths, all inside the claim as amended by 6884227999. No breach. `content/docs/deployment/validating-metadata.mdx` is not edited; the body says why.
- **Gate not measured by the dev** (`check:dual-build-cjs-loads`): CI's. No check-run on this head failed; which job carries it was not traced.

**S1, should-fix, escalated to the seat. "Never null" holds for a stored row; a `beforeInsert` hook ordered ahead of the stamp reads `null`.**
